entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: We have perused the impugned Judgment and Order.
We have also perused the notes of evidence which are annexed along with the Application.

2. At the outset, we must mention that the Accused was convicted for the offence under Section 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012, the Accused was sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for seven years and pay fine of Rs.3,000/-.
This according to us is itself sufficient to infer that the Judgment and Order dated 14/06/2023 requires re- consideration.

It is pertinent to note that the minimum imprisonment which is prescribed under Section 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012 is ten years, thus imposing sentence of seven years itself raises doubt about correctness of the impugned Judgment and Order.
The evidence of the Prosecutrix is annexed by the Applicant at Page no.50 of the present 20-ALS(ST)-728-2025.doc Application.
We have perused the said evidence.
In addition to that we have also perused the evidence of the Medical Officer.
We are satisfied that this is a fit case for grant of leave to file Appeal.
3. Accordingly, leave to file Appeal against the Judgment and Order dated 14/06/2023 is granted.
4. Appeal be registered.
5. Action under Section 431 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 be taken.
6. Notice for enhancement of the sentence is issued.

7. Application for Leave to Appeal (ST.) No. 728 of 2025 is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
(SANDESH D. PATIL, J.) (SARANG V. KOTWAL, J.)
